brief:
Recent messages in Kevin's Hermes chat (newest last):
Kevin: remind me, when's the dentist?
Hermes: Your dentist appointment is Friday at 3:30 pm with Dr. Patel.
Kevin: nice. what's a good weeknight dinner that isn't pasta
Hermes: A sheet-pan chicken thigh dinner works well: toss thighs, sliced onion and chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt, roast at 425 F for about 30 minutes, then finish with lemon and yogurt. One pan, little prep, and leftovers reheat fine for lunch.
Kevin: what's a good way to keep houseplants alive when I travel for a week
Hermes: Water deeply the day you leave, group the plants together away from direct sun so they lose less water, and set the thirstier ones on a tray of wet pebbles. For a week that is usually enough; for longer trips a self-watering spike or a wick from a jar of water works.
Kevin: and Harsha's flight?
Hermes: Harsha's flight UA 1184 lands at 6:40 pm at Austin airport, terminal A.
Kevin: what's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore again
Hermes: A mutex is a lock with an owner: one thread takes it, the same thread releases it, and it guards one critical section. A semaphore is a counter: it lets up to N holders in at once and any thread can signal it, so it fits pools of identical resources or signalling between threads. A binary semaphore looks like a mutex but has no ownership, which is why priority inheritance only applies to mutexes.
Kevin: what did we cap the Tokyo trip at
Hermes: The Tokyo trip budget is $1,800 for flights and hotel, food separate.
Kevin: is it worth learning rust for small cli tools
Hermes: For small CLI tools it pays off if you want a single static binary, fast startup and no runtime to install; clap and anyhow make the boring parts short. The cost is a slower first week fighting the borrow checker. If the tools are glue around other programs, a shell or Python script is still faster to write and change.
Kevin: which voice engine is default now
Hermes: GPT-Live is the default voice engine. Grok Voice is switchable; on the frozen bench Grok passed 24 of 24 runs and GPT-Live 17 of 24.
Kevin: summarize the idea behind CRDTs in two sentences
Hermes: CRDTs are data types designed so that replicas can accept edits independently and still converge to the same state when they exchange updates, without a central coordinator. They do it by making the merge operation commutative, associative and idempotent, so the order and repetition of updates never matter.
Kevin: how much memory does the studio have
Hermes: The Mac Studio is an M5 Max with 36 GB of unified memory and about 217 GB of free disk.
Kevin: ok. also you have my OK to read my phone screen over adb during calls.
Hermes: Noted: adb screen access during calls is approved.
Kevin: what's the best way to learn a bit of Japanese before a trip
Hermes: Learn hiragana and katakana first, which takes about two weeks of short daily sessions and lets you read menus and signs. Then add a phrasebook set of 50 polite survival phrases and practice them out loud with audio. A spaced-repetition app for ten minutes a day keeps it from fading.
